topic.title: Inductive Learning on Relational Graphs
topic.overview: Relational learning predicts links and answers queries using the pattern of connections among entities. This topic emphasizes generalization to new entities, relations, or databases rather than memorizing one fixed graph. Relation graphs, structural representations, and learned graph construction help models reuse relational patterns across changing data.
topic.whyItMatters: A knowledge base or database evolves after training. Systems that depend on a separate learned embedding for every known entity can struggle when new objects arrive, making inductive structure essential for reusable reasoning.
topic.evolution: Earlier work explores hierarchical relational embeddings and graph-based concepts. The 2019–2023 representatives focus on long-range dependencies, subgraph reasoning, and logical queries over unseen entities and relations. Recent database work asks which graph representation actually supports the downstream task, balancing removal of irrelevant structure against addition of useful connections.
openQuestions: Which relational patterns transfer when both entity types and relation vocabularies change?
How can graph optimization preserve semantics while simplifying computation?

papers.tldr: OHD represents complex tables through complementary row and column trees to preserve the hierarchical meaning needed for question answering.

papers.title: PluRel: Synthetic Data unlocks Scaling Laws for Relational Foundation Models
papers.tldr: PluRel generates diverse connected databases, revealing empirical scaling laws and improved transfer from synthetic pretraining to real relational data.

papers.title: Ramba: Selective State-Space Models for Relational Deep Learning
papers.tldr: Ramba combines selective state-space processing with relational structure and schema-aware gating to learn efficiently across database tables.

papers.title: Rel-MOSS: Towards Imbalanced Relational Deep Learning on Relational Databases
papers.tldr: Rel-MOSS improves imbalanced database classification through relation-specific message control and relationally consistent synthetic minority examples.

papers.title: Relational In-Context Learning via Synthetic Pre-training with Structural Prior
papers.tldr: RDB-PFN learns from synthetic relational tasks and transfers through in-context learning to strong few-shot prediction on real databases.

papers.title: Unsat Core Prediction through Polarity-Aware Representation Learning over Clause-Literal Hypergraphs
papers.tldr: A polarity-aware hypergraph framework improves SAT representation learning by explicitly modeling clause interactions and positive-negative literal relationships.

papers.title: What Makes a Desired Graph for Relational Deep Learning?
papers.tldr: Task-aware removal and addition of graph structure improves relational prediction, with optimized graphs often reducing inference cost.
